content.value_statement: Next.js teams often mix page, layout, routing, and data fetching patterns. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concise project conventions.
actual_capabilities: Explains where App Router pages and layouts belong.
Guides when to use Server Components or Client Components.
Recommends Link and useRouter for Next.js navigation.
Describes server and client data fetching choices.
Covers next/font/google and metadata placement for SEO.
limitations: Covers conventions only, not a full migration plan.
Does not include testing, deployment, or performance tuning guidance.
Assumes a Next.js 15 App Router project.
Does not define repository-specific route names or UI requirements.

use_cases.title: Create App Router Pages
use_cases.description: Build pages and layouts that follow the expected Next.js file structure.

use_cases.title: Review Routing Choices
use_cases.description: Check whether navigation uses Link or useRouter in the right component context.

use_cases.title: Standardize Project Patterns
use_cases.description: Align team guidance for components, data fetching, fonts, and metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new App Router page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the next-js-patterns skill to plan a new App Router page for this feature. Include page location, component type, and navigation needs.

prompt_templates.title: Check Component Boundary
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of server and client component usage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the next-js-patterns skill to review this component. Tell me whether it should be a Server Component or Client Component and why.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Navigation Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate routing review for user flows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the next-js-patterns skill to review this navigation flow. Recommend Link or useRouter for each navigation action.

prompt_templates.title: Audit App Router Conventions
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across pages, layouts, data fetching, fonts, and metadata.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the next-js-patterns skill to audit this Next.js feature. Check routing, layouts, component boundaries, data fetching, fonts, and metadata.

output_examples.input: Review a dashboard page that uses browser state and navigation.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies that the page needs a Client Component boundary and recommends programmatic navigation only inside that boundary.

output_examples.input: Plan metadata and font usage for a marketing route.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends placing metadata in the route file or layout and using next/font/google from the root layout.

output_examples.input: Check a product detail page for data fetching choices.
output_examples.output: The assistant suggests server-side fetching for initial data and client-side fetching only for browser-driven updates.

best_practices: Default to Server Components unless browser APIs or state are required.
Use Link for internal links and useRouter for client-side programmatic navigation.
Place shared wrappers, fonts, and metadata in the appropriate layout file.
anti_patterns: Adding use client to every component without a browser requirement.
Putting route metadata in unrelated components instead of page or layout files.

faq.question: Does this skill support the App Router?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on Next.js 15 App Router pages, layouts, routing, and related conventions.

faq.question: Does it generate complete features by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance that an AI assistant can apply while working in a project.

faq.question: When should a component use use client?
faq.answer: Use it when the component needs state, effects, browser APIs, or client-only navigation behavior.

faq.question: What navigation APIs does it recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends Link for internal navigation and useRouter for programmatic navigation in Client Components.

faq.question: Does it cover SEO metadata?
faq.answer: Yes. It reminds assistants to define metadata in page or layout files where appropriate.

faq.question: Can Claude Code and Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
